This tab contains usable records for the website sections in data gathering, plus explicit gaps where the public pages do not supply the requested fields. It is a source-backed starting dataset, not a complete current directory of every city service, official, facility, or route. The original data gathering tab is unchanged.
Category status measures coverage of the data requested in data gathering. Evidence labels measure the strength and age of individual records.
— All requested fields for that category or explicitly named subdataset are collected, sourced and checked; no material gaps remain.
— Some usable data is collected, but requested fields, directory coverage or current versions are still missing.
— The requested usable dataset has not been obtained. Identifying a source portal alone does not complete the dataset.
— Available material is provisional or lacks the authoritative or current confirmation required for use.
— Verified: stated by the cited primary source. Dated: tied to its stated year/event. Provisional: needs confirmation. Missing: not retrieved. Verified does not mean complete or current.
Overall coverage of the 20 requested categories
— 0 complete, 18 partial, 1 missing and 1 needs verification. Complete subdatasets are identified within the relevant category status.
Statuses refer to the material documented in this tab, not website implementation progress. A retrieval date does not change a record’s reference year; source IDs refer to the source register.
— Population counts for 2010, 2015, 2020 and 2024 are complete; 2024 households, demographic breakdowns and CPDO indicators remain missing.
Use the 2024 census for the population card. The city homepage still cites 2015; do not label that figure current. Sources

• PSA yearbook basis; CPDO boundary basis not obtained

Derived values, calculated from the cited counts: population increased by 20,524 people, or 4.43%, between the 2020 and 2024 censuses. Using 63.37 km² gives about 7,629 persons/km² for 2024; this is our calculation, not a quoted CPDO indicator. Keep area basis alongside density.
Missing: extracted 2024 household count and household population, age and sex breakdowns, city poverty and employment indicators, CPDO projections and approved land-use figures.
identifies the 2024 household dataset but its selector page did not expose the Angeles values; retain the 2020 labels until extracted.

. Columns are official name, 10-digit PSGC, and 2024 POPCEN population. Preserve accents and spelling; keep codes as strings. Do not substitute school-directory spellings for PSGC names.

Barangay captains and directory telephone values

Source S56: region III barangay officials list.xlsx, Sheet1, rows 10627–11279, columns A–L; filtered by CITY/MUNICIPALITY = CITY OF ANGELES. The workbook contains 653 Angeles official records, including 33 captains; all carry TERM = 2023 - 2026. No publication date or issuer is stated in the extracted worksheet. These are transcribed directory records, not independently confirmed current appointments or working phone lines.

The source column is headed BARANGAY TEL NO. The main table preserves the value on each captain’s row; it does not establish that the number is the captain’s personal/direct number. Thirteen captain rows contain numeric phone values. NONE, N/A and 0 remain explicit gaps. Seven-digit landlines retain their source form; no area code is guessed.

— Selected heritage facts are sourced; a complete founding-to-cityhood timeline has not been collected.

Verified heritage facts suitable for short original summaries: Holy Rosary Church construction was completed on 12 February 1896. The building now housing Museo ning Angeles was constructed in 1922 and transferred to Kuliat Foundation in 1999. Sources

NHCP records Pamintuan Mansion as built in the 1890s, used by the Philippine Republic in 1899, and inaugurated as the Museum of Philippine Social History on 24 August 2015. Its historical marker dates to 17 August 2017. Source

For website copy, use NHCP for the mansion’s construction and historical dates. The tourism page and NHCP describe its builder differently; do not silently merge their accounts. A fully sourced founding-to-cityhood timeline was not extracted.

7 Business permits and local taxes — PARTIAL
— The permit charter, form and workflow are collected. Conflicting checklists need BPLD confirmation; current fees, help contacts and 2026 tax guidance are missing.
Service: online issuance of a business permit. Responsible office: BPLD / Business One-Stop Shop. Audience: businesses and authorized requesting parties. Portal:
; the city homepage links it, but the portal itself could not be fetched during collection.

New application baseline: eApplication; registration/legal-personality proof; occupancy permit where applicable; lease if renting; barangay clearance; cedula. Renewal baseline: eApplication, barangay clearance, cedula, fire-safety certification and prior-year tax/sales evidence. Business-specific additions apply. Source

Steps: register and activate by email; choose new application or link an existing Business ID for renewal; complete the form and upload documents; choose pickup/delivery; submit; monitor email and correct deficiencies; check assessment; pay through Landbank Link.Biz; print the ePermit. Source

Fees depend on assessed receipts/capital and the applicable schedule; no single fixed fee was verified. Charter turnaround is three working days if payment occurs within that period. Pickup address, current help contact, fee schedule and category-specific checklist were not retrieved. Source
Downloadable form: BPLD-ABP-001 Rev 33, dated 1 October 2025,

. It separately lists BFP certification and conditional occupancy/barangay requirements. The form and charter differ in details; retain both source checklists and have BPLD reconcile them before publishing one definitive checklist.

Local tax record, Provisional index-only extraction: the Treasurer’s calendar-2024 notice states 2% basic real property tax plus 1% SEF tax, with quarterly due dates ending March 31, June 30, September 30 and December 31, 2024.
returned 403 on full-document access. This is a historical source lead, not verified 2026 guidance; current rates, discounts, assessment basis and deadlines remain Missing.
— Health ID guidance and six TB-program health-unit locations are collected. Full licensed-facility coverage, schedules and several service fields are missing; published hours need confirmation.

Health ID / sanitary ID: the city portal offers registration and appointment slots. Its baseline list is chest X-ray result/film valid six months, urinalysis/fecalysis valid two weeks, current-year cedula and appointment slip. Arrive 15 minutes before the booked time. Source

, adds Hepatitis A IgM for food handlers and notarized parental consent for applicants aged 17 or below. It lists extra TESDA/STI-HIV certificates for massage therapists and drug screening, STI-HIV training and a signed hiring/offer letter for non-CCA entertainment workers. Confirm the checklist for the applicant’s category. The form is free; no service fee was verified.
. The 5 February 2026 advisory identifies Jessie Paul M. Culang as City Health Physician/OIC; retain that date rather than asserting a current appointment.

The portal lists EHS at 3rd floor City Hall, Pulung Maragul, Monday–Friday 08:00–19:00 except holidays. Treat hours as published and needing office confirmation: the city also has a newer compressed-workweek notice,
. Its SM Clark site window ended 30 April 2026 and is not an active schedule. Fees and turnaround were not stated. Source

DPWH record 25CI0039 concerns construction of the Abacan Road Dike between Henson Bridge and Abacan Bridge, Angeles City. A DPWH award-document search extract states ₱94,374,619.06 and approval on 14 March 2025. Source

Local infrastructure example: Pampang Public Market redevelopment, reported city cost ₱400 million, with an inauguration scheduled for 29 November 2024. The report describes three floors, 200 dry-goods stalls, 50 side-wing stalls and 251 parking spaces. Source
. This is a dated city announcement; it is not a completion certificate or current project-progress report.

Verified source destinations: PAGASA heat index

Static climate context: PAGASA’s Clark rainfall-normal row gives monthly rainfall in mm as Jan 17.4; Feb 18.6; Mar 28.4; Apr 65.0; May 221.8; Jun 241.2; Jul 422.6; Aug 429.4; Sep 293.1; Oct 177.0; Nov 78.0; Dec 34.2; annual 2,026.8. Source
. These are long-term station normals, not observed 2026 rainfall or a citywide forecast; confirm the underlying normal period before chart publication.

For implementation, retain station identifier, observed/forecast distinction, issue time, valid-until time, units and source URL. Clark airport observations are a nearby station proxy and should not be labeled a measurement at every Angeles barangay. A supported public data API and refresh contract were not verified.
— GIS datasets have not been obtained: boundaries, zoning, hazard layers and facility/transport/project geometry are missing. Source portals and address leads are identified only.
Geoportal Philippines exposes layer search, WMS discovery, active faults and flood-hazard layers,
. HazardHunterPH is a multi-agency hazard-assessment tool,
, and PHIVOLCS provides hazard-map download guidance,

Collected here: source destinations and facility addresses suitable for geocoding. Not extracted: barangay polygons, official city boundary, zoning or land-use GIS files, flood raster/vector files, evacuation points, markets, terminals, parking, road closures or project geometry.

Request CPDO’s approved boundary/zoning files with edition date, coordinate reference system, coverage and reuse terms. For each map layer record its agency, scale, vintage, CRS and license. Do not draw boundaries or hazard areas from place names, infer safe evacuation areas, or treat a web map screenshot as downloadable GIS.

contains an October 2026 compressed-workweek advisory and a La Naval class/work suspension notice. Keep historical suspension notices out of a current-alert banner after expiry. Culture sources: CKS hosts Singsing magazine, Alaya research journals, Kapampangan-language materials and a translator with English/Filipino inputs,
. The translator is a community-contributed work in progress. No dictionary entries, Kulitan character mappings or quiz answers were extracted from its query interface.

For Kulitan, obtain a reviewed primary teaching/reference source. For the trivia game, the verified church, museum and mansion dates above can form cited questions; avoid unsupported founding dates or etymologies.
21 Data gaps and publication readiness — PARTIAL
— The gap register is documented, but the overall dataset is not ready for publication as a complete current city directory. Complete subdatasets can be used with their dates and source limits.

Ready as dated factual content: PSA population and barangay rows; short sourced heritage facts; source links; reported project and procurement records with their amount types and dates. The verified mayor record can seed the officials page with a last-checked date.

Needs confirmation before service guidance: BPLD checklist differences, fee schedules and help contacts; EHS hours under the compressed workweek; museum hours/fees; local hotlines; current private-school authority; live event changes.

Not collected: complete current officials and department directories; remaining barangay telephone gaps, emails, addresses and facilities; citywide service procedures; full school and hospital inventories; waste schedule; GIS files; official jeepney routing; budget/audit exports; current project progress; reusable dictionary/Kulitan dataset. These are deliberately left Missing, not estimated.

Office follow-up package: CPDO—city profile, CLUP/zoning and barangay GIS plus project inventory; HRMO/SP/Barangay Affairs—dated officials, offices and contacts; each service office—latest charter, forms, schedules and fees; CHO/DOH—facility registry; DepEd—current complete school list; CENRO—collection calendar; ACDRRMO—facility and evacuation roster; ACTDO/LTFRB—authorized routes and fares; Budget/Accounting/Treasurer/BAC—financial and procurement files; ACTO/CKS—visitor calendar and reusable cultural content.

Recommended ingestion fields for every record: id, section, raw_name, display_name, value, unit, reference_date, source_url, source_title, retrieved_at, verification_status and notes. Keep monetary values numeric with currency PHP, phone numbers as strings and unknown values null. Preserve raw values alongside normalized ones.
— Source references S01–S56 are documented. This indicates citation coverage only; inaccessible sources and missing data remain flagged in their categories.
